unit.title: Agents for teachers’ work, checked and approved

lesson.title: Ask clearly
lesson.subtitle: The goal, the details, the limits, and what done looks like

video.title: Ask clearly
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: Four parts of a clear request

scenes.visual: A list: “The thing, next week”; Which thing? Which day? What time?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I told our school agent: remind me about the thing next week. It answered with three questions. Which thing, which day, what time? Fair enough, really.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how to ask an agent clearly.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Vague in, questions or guesses out
scenes.narration: An agent can only act on what you write. When a detail is missing, a good agent asks, like Darsi Tiny asking which village. A weaker one guesses, and a guess can be wrong.

scenes.visual: A list: Goal: what you want done; Details: who, what, when, where; Limits: what it must not do; Done: what you will check.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A clear request has four parts. The goal, what you want done. The details: who, what, when and where. The limits, what it must not do. And what done looks like, so you can check it.

scenes.visual: A list: Vague: tell the parents about the trip; Clear: a draft for 6B’s parents; Friday’s farm trip is cancelled; Show me before sending.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A vague one: tell the parents about the trip. A clear one: draft a message to six B’s parents saying Friday’s farm trip is cancelled, and show me before sending. The clear one has a goal, details, a limit and a finish line.

scenes.visual: A list: Which page; Who needs help; What not to start yet; It can’t read your mind.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Like a note for a supply teacher
scenes.narration: It’s like the note you leave for a supply teacher: which page, who needs help, and what not to start yet. An agent needs that note every time. It can’t read your mind.

scenes.visual: A list: “Don’t send it yet”; Words are a request, not a lock; The app asks before any action.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A limit in words isn’t a lock
scenes.narration: Limits matter most. Words like don’t send it yet tell the agent where to stop. But a limit in words is a request, not a lock. A good app backs it up by asking you before any action.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Which of these requests will an agent get right the first time?

scenes.visual: A list: Goal: a reminder; Monday, 7:30, 6B, science; Nothing to guess or ask.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The Monday one. It has the goal, a reminder, and every detail: the day, the time, the class and the subject. There’s nothing left to guess or to ask. And afterwards, it’s easy to check.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Wording matters too. With wordings it learned, Darsi Tiny gets the tool and every detail right nearly every time; with new wordings, about four times in five. Plain, complete requests help every agent.

scenes.visual: A list: Role; Task; Context: your class; Format.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: build a better prompt
scenes.narration: In the app, build a request from parts: a role, a task, the context and a format. Ask with two parts, then add the context and watch the answer fit your class.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. I asked: what’s the weather tomorrow. What will a good agent do?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Goal, details, limits, done; Missing details: it asks or guesses; Limits need the app too.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Goal, details, limits, done · Missing details: it asks or guesses · Limits need the app too
scenes.narration: It asks which village, because a detail is missing. Remember: a clear request has a goal, details, limits and what done looks like. Missing details make an agent ask, or guess. And a limit in words should be backed up by the app.

scenes.visual: A list: Play “Vague to clear”; Rewrite: goal, details, limits, done; The agent does only what’s written; Where did it guess?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play Vague to clear. Pairs write a vague request, then rewrite it with a goal, details, limits and a finish line. A partner plays the agent and does only what is written. Where did the agent have to guess?

checkpoints.prompt: Which request will an agent get right the first time?

options.text: “Remind me on Monday at 7:30 to collect 6B’s science homework.”

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it has the goal and every detail: the day, the time, the class and the subject. Nothing is left to guess.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the other two leave out the day, the time or the class, so the agent has to ask or guess.

checkpoints.prompt: You ask: “What’s the weather tomorrow?” What will a good agent do?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the village is missing, so a good agent asks instead of guessing. Darsi Tiny answers “Which village?”.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a guess could be wrong. The village is missing, so a good agent asks which one.
